articles.headline: Claude-shaped science
articles.blurb: Matthew Schwartz describes using AI, notably Claude, to tackle "Claude-shaped" scientific problems where LLM capabilities like coding and data parsing excel. This led to BootLoops, a toolkit facilitating quantitative science calculations across diverse fields from ecology to population genetics. Despite initial technical correctness, results required domain experts to refine relevance, illustrating that AI collaborations can rapidly produce technical solutions but still depend on human insight for impactful scientific advances.

The company has launched MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming along with MAI‑Voice‑2.1 and MAI‑Voice‑2.1-Flash, giving users fast and fluid building blocks to create conversational experiences with no compromise on accuracy or voice quality. The model only scores supplied options and doesn't generate explanations or retrieve missing facts. The code, weights, and evaluation reports are available, but the full 27B training corpus and some evaluation data are private.

articles.headline: The Waymo effect: how AI is quietly making research less collaborative

Funding structures and evaluation systems exacerbate this shift by rewarding speed and output over collaborative effort, risking the degradation of rich, human-driven research culture.

articles.headline: Row-level security performance in PostgreSQL, measured
articles.blurb: PostgreSQL row-level security can be effectively free when the policy is a simple indexed tenant check, but poorly structured policies can turn sub-millisecond queries into tens of milliseconds or even seconds. The main traps are per-row membership lookups, VOLATILE helper functions, and non-leakproof query functions that stop PostgreSQL from using the full index.

articles.headline: Rebuilding Data Engineering with Harness Engineering: A New Paradigm for the Agent Era
articles.blurb: Data platforms are shifting from human-operated tooling to agent-ready infrastructure, where the core challenge is not generating SQL or pipelines but safely turning AI-generated work into production outcomes. The proposed stack centers on five layers: Intent, Control, Semantic, Harness, and Runtime. For data teams, the implication is a move from building scripts and DAGs to designing reusable Skills, Policies, and context-rich execution loops that make automation trustworthy.

articles.headline: Improving Cost Efficiency of Data Streaming Pipelines
articles.blurb: Streaming platforms get expensive for structural reasons, not data volume: request counts, extra copies of each message, serialization, and cross-AZ traffic often dominate the bill. Practical wins include batching producers and consumers, eliminating intermediate topics, using columnar payloads and compression, paying for low latency only where workloads truly need it, designing state deliberately, and keeping cost attribution visible per pipeline.

articles.headline: Can Your LLM Vibe Code Your Semantic Layer?
articles.blurb: A strong semantic layer can dramatically improve LLM analytics accuracy, with the best model-built layer reaching 91% versus 39% with no layer. The main failure mode was not metric arithmetic but hidden business conventions like which accounts count as customers, showing that semantic layers still need explicit human-defined rules and validation.

articles.headline: RIP, vector database
articles.blurb: turbopuffer v3 stops using the ANN vector index as the primary storage layout. That should reduce duplicated data and expensive rewrites, while letting full-text, filtering, aggregations, and vector search each use storage and block sizes better suited to their workload.

articles.headline: Handling hot shards
articles.blurb: Sharding by tenant ID works until a large tenant makes one shard run hot, as Slack learned when enterprise workspaces overwhelmed workspace-keyed shards. The fixes range from vertical scaling to isolating whale tenants on dedicated shards and ultimately resharding tables by the column queries actually touch. Choosing keys per table rather than globally keeps common access paths single-shard while spreading load.

articles.headline: The Five Camps of Data Modeling (and Which One You're Stuck In)
articles.blurb: Data modeling grew up in five separate camps: relational, analytics, application, ML/AI, and knowledge/ontology, each solving different problems with real blind spots. One JSON product catalog can satisfy an application while breaking analytics, ML, and governance, producing brittle pipelines and lost dashboard trust. Modern stacks span all five camps at once, so shared literacy across them matters more than any single modeling tradition.

articles.headline: Parquet X-ray (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Parquet X-ray is a browser-based visual inspector for understanding how a Parquet file is physically laid out. You can open a local file or remote URL and explore row groups, column chunks, pages, indexes, bloom filters, schema, min/max statistics, compression efficiency, and byte-level layout without downloading the whole file. You can test it out via Hugging Face.

articles.headline: Splink 5: Probabilistic record linkage at billion-row scale
articles.blurb: Splink, an open-source library for record linkage and deduplication, scales probabilistic record linkage to billion-row jobs: a prediction job ran 10 billion comparisons in 8.5 minutes on a 192-vCPU instance using the upcoming DuckDB 2.0 engine. The tool supports chunked sampling to speed up model training or distribute processing and incremental prediction APIs to link new records without full re-runs.

articles.headline: A Hint of Dependence
articles.blurb: Query hints solve bad plans by hard-coding execution choices into SQL, which creates brittle coupling to indexes and data shape. A better approach is to keep plan control outside the query and improve the planner's information with tools like plan management and CREATE STATISTICS, so it can adapt as the data changes.

articles.headline: Anthropic says it fixed Claude's writing. I ran the evals to check

The bigger lesson is methodological: style evals work better when you annotate exact problematic spans and judge recurring rhetorical moves, not just banned phrases or vague overall scores.

Shadowserver found 274 compromised instances.

articles.headline: Fortinet warns of critical FortiMail flaw exploited in zero-day attacks
articles.blurb: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-104286 as a zero-day, a CVSS 9.8 path traversal and NULL byte flaw in the FortiMail management interface that lets unauthenticated HTTP requests write arbitrary files and execute code. FortiMail 7.2.0 through 8.0.1 is affected, and fixed builds 7.4.9, 7.6.7, and 8.0.2 are not yet available, so admins should disable IBE or restrict the management interface to trusted networks. Compromise indicators include an added /data/etc/ld.so.preload and /data/lib/liblog.so, plus an archive account named archive234 pointing to 79[.]141[.]169[.]187, and CISA gave federal agencies until October 4 to triage and mitigate.

articles.headline: Revenge of the SD-WAN: Exploring and Exploiting Yet Another Critical Cisco SD-WAN Vulnerability (CVE-2026-76504)
articles.blurb: A single unauthenticated POST to /%6a_security_check mints an admin session on Cisco SD-WAN vManage through CVE-2026-76504, a critical authentication bypass Cisco disclosed on September 30 as an exploited zero-day. Cisco's login module checked the raw request URI while WildFly matched the decoded path, so the encoded request skipped the password check and fell into a session-continuation branch that trusted hardcoded internal usernames like viptela-reserved-cloudops. With ~1,500 vManage instances internet-exposed per VulnCheck, defenders should follow Cisco's advisory and hunt serviceproxy-access.log and vmanage-server.log for encoded j_security_check paths and viptela-reserved- usernames.

articles.headline: Solving the Identity Crisis for AI Agents
articles.blurb: Uber faced two issues with agentic identity: its current identity model wasn't designed to account for agents acting on behalf of users, and provenance wasn't properly carried across different agents in a workflow. To address this, Uber implemented an identity system in which workflows begin by requesting a workload ID from SPIRE. That ID is then presented to a custom STS, which verifies in its agent registry that the requested agent is allowed to run on that workflow and returns a JWT with the relevant details to the workload. To simplify adoption, Uber built a standardized Agent-to-Agent client that provides an automatic, secure-by-default path.

articles.headline: What We Should Do Instead of Trusted Cyber Access Programs and Open Weight Restrictions
articles.blurb: It is pivotal to provide defenders with access to the most powerful, cyber-capable models, whether open-weight or frontier models. Instead of restricting access to these models, we should shift the paradigm to focus more on restricting attackers' access. Frontier labs should implement low-friction, cross-lab Know Your Customer (KYC) programs, do more to detect and block attackers, and publish time-to-detection-and-response metrics. Victims of AI cyberattacks should also be encouraged to share more detailed information about the attack and the attackers.

articles.headline: Bitget hacked via zero-day in third-party security products
articles.blurb: A zero-day in a third-party security product gave Bitget's attacker a foothold on August 31, 25 days before the $387.5 million theft. The attacker later planted a web shell and C2 on a second appliance and pivoted to the production wallet job server, where a custom withdrawal tool forged risk-control parameters and drained wallets in under three hours. The vendors remain unnamed, and the North Korea attribution comes only from Bitget's CEO, so the takeaway is to monitor security appliances like production hosts and enforce withdrawal risk checks outside the wallet host.

Operators replayed encrypted reasoning and used cross-conversation prompts, with OpenAI linking a core cluster to Moonshot AI personnel, restricted accounts, closed replay paths, added output checks, and shared indicators with partners.

High-risk flaws rose 167%, and exploited vulnerabilities averaged 18 per month, up from 10.5 in 2025. AI-discovered bugs more often enable remote code execution (50% vs 26%) and skew toward medium and low risk. Researchers saw rapid weaponization of n-days, including a BeyondTrust flaw exploited within four days of disclosure. AI-related CVEs also climbed, with 2,076 tracked since early 2025, though zero-days against AI infrastructure remain unconfirmed.

articles.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight
